title: Scarlett Johansson warns about the dangers of AI after Kanye West Deepfake goes viral
text:
Scarlett Johansson has warned about the “imminent dangers of AI” after a video of his deep defense and other prominent Jewish celebrities that oppose the recent antisemy comments of Kanye West became viral this week.
The video contained versions generated by the more than a dozen celebrities, including Johansson, David Schwimmer, Jerry Seinfeld, Drake, Adam Sandler, Stephen Spielberg and Mila Kunis.
It opened with a deep similarity of Johansson in a shirt that was stamped with an extended half -hand and finger, a star of David and Kanye’s name. The video was established in “Hava Nagila”, a Jewish popular song that usually reproduces in cultural celebration events, and ended with the slogan: “Enough is enough. Join the fight against anti -Semitism.”
Other stars represented included Sacha Baron Cohen, Jack Black, Natalie Portman, Adam Levine, Ben Stiller and Lenny Kravitz.
“Family members and friends have caught my attention, that a video generated by AI with my similarity, in response to an anti -Semitic vision, has circulated online and gaining ground,” said Johansson. In a statement to people .
“I am a Jewish woman who has no tolerance to anti -Semitism or the hate discourse of any kind. But I also firmly believe that the potential for hate discourse multiplied by AI is a much greater threat than any person who will appear responsibility. We must call the misuse of AI, regardless of their messages, or we run the risk of losing reality. “
West, now known as Ye, repeatedly referred to himself as a “Nazi” and praised Hitler in X before deactivating his account.
It also appeared in an ad during the Super Bowl that directed people to their website, which began selling only one product: t -shirts with swastika in them. The site was removed by Shopify due to policy violations, while Fox Television Stations, Jack Abernethy, also also condemned the announcement in a note to the staff .
Johansson has been one of the most vocal celebrities against the use of AI without consent. Last year, he threatened legal actions against Operai after the company used a voice that looked like its in its new Chatgpt product, nine months after he said he rejected the company’s request to express its AI system.
Operai finally eliminated the very promoted voice option of chatgpt after a generalized reaction.
Johansson said he had been “a very public victim of AI, but the truth is that the threat of the affects each and every one of us.”
She added: “There is a 1,000 feet wave with respect to the AI ​​that several progressive countries, not including the United States, have responded responsible. It is terrifying that the United States government is paralyzed when it comes to passing legislation that protects all its citizens against the imminent dangers of AI. “
The actor urged elected officials to take legislative measures against AI abuses, describing it as “a bipartisan problem that greatly affects the immediate future of humanity in general.”
Their comments come when the United Kingdom’s advertising standards authority said false ads with celebrities It is still the most common type of scam ads appearing online.
The video of AI was created by Ori Bejrano, who describes himself as a generative expert of AI in his Instagram biography . Its original publication included a notice that said that the content was “created digitally or altered with AI to seem real.”
